title: Recall
description: Closed-book memory of exact public-domain text, speeches and music: how much is right, how much is invented, and whether the model knows which.

values.label: Literature
values.description: Exact passages of public-domain prose, poetry and scripture.

values.label: Speeches
values.description: Historic speeches; scored against the best-matching accepted version.

values.label: Music
values.description: Passages written out as a score (ABC or MusicXML), part by part.

metrics.label: Accuracy
metrics.description: Share of reference words (or notes) reproduced.

metrics.label: Invention
metrics.description: Share of answer words that are inserted or wrong (gap markers excluded).

metrics.label: Brier
metrics.description: Calibration: Brier score of per-line confidence (0 = perfect).

metrics.label: 2nd attempt
metrics.description: Change in item score after one unprompted self-review.

metrics.label: Best guess
metrics.description: Item score when the model was asked to fill its gaps with its best guess (music only; the headline stays the honest first answer).

metrics.label: Confident-wrong
metrics.description: In the best-guess answer, the share of bars the model gave 70+ confidence that were wrong.

scoring: Closed book: the seat has no tools, no shell and no web search, and the transcript is checked afterwards; any tool call voids the item. A refusal is recorded as refused, not as a recall failure.
The seat writes the passage out with a 0-100 confidence per line (or bar) and marks gaps instead of guessing. Answers are aligned word by word (note by note for music) against the reference.
Item score = accuracy x (1 - invention rate), 0-100. Calibration (Brier score, expected calibration error) is reported alongside, not folded in.
caveats: Seat = model + effort + harness. Claude seats run in Claude Code, GPT seats in the Codex CLI, so model and harness are confounded.
Seats run with the fleet's own agent configuration (instructions, skills and hooks), not a vanilla install of Claude Code or the Codex CLI.
All runs used the fleet's subscription logins except the older API baselines (GPT-4o, o3, GPT-5), which ran pay-per-token on the OpenAI API with a per-run cost cap.

Cost is a list-price figure, not what was paid. Claude Code reports its own list-price cost; the Codex CLI reports only tokens, so GPT costs are estimates from token counts at published list prices (standard tier; one price was taken from third-party trackers).
One capped Opus 4.5 run (FIX-01) reported no cost; its figure is estimated from transcript tokens at list price.
Some speeches exist in several accepted versions; the seat is scored against the best-matching one.
Memorisation is the point here, so contamination is not a flaw. One private item is scored but never published.
